subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Hydraulic Turbines: Power from Falling Water
description: One-minute skill: Hydraulic Turbines: Power from Falling Water.

hook.text: Water falls from a dam and spins a turbine. Gravity does the work.

buildup.text: Falling water gains speed. The turbine converts that speed to shaft power.

discovery.text: Different heads need different turbines — Pelton, Francis, or Kaplan.

twist.text: Hydro turbines can hit 95% efficiency — the highest of any turbine type.

climax.text: Hoover Dam's turbines produce enough power for 1.3 million people.

punchline.text: Gravity plus water equals clean power forever.

quiz.question: Why are different turbine designs used for different dam heights?
options: Higher dams need bigger generators to handle the voltage
Different heads produce different flow patterns needing matched blade designs
Taller dams require turbines that spin more slowly
